questions.q: A sponge is squeezed. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: Squeezing the sponge makes it flatter. This shows that a force can change the shape of an object.

questions.q: A ball is still on the ground. It is kicked. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: The ball was still before the kick and moving after it. This shows that a force can make a still object start moving.

questions.q: A hockey stick hits a moving ball to one side. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: The ball was already moving, and the hit sends it off to one side. This shows that a force can change the direction of a moving object.

questions.q: A goalkeeper catches a moving ball. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: The goalkeeper's hands push against the moving ball until it stops. This shows that a force can stop a moving object.

questions.q: A cyclist brakes and the bicycle slows down. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: The brakes make the bicycle go slower. This shows that a force can change the speed of a moving object.

questions.q: A door is pushed and swings on its hinges. Identify the effect of the force.
questions.explain: The hinges act as a pivot, and the push makes the door turn about them. This shows that a force can turn an object about a pivot.

questions.q: A force can change the shape of an object. Identify the example of this.
questions.explain: Pressing a lump of clay squashes it into a new shape. Pushing a door turns it, braking slows a bicycle, and catching stops a ball.

questions.q: A force can turn an object. Name the turning effect of a force.
questions.explain: The turning effect of a force is called a moment. The pivot is the point that the object turns about.

questions.q: A moment depends on the size of the force. State the other factor.
questions.explain: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot. So the moment depends on the size of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.

questions.q: The same force pushes a door further from its hinge. Predict the change in moment.
questions.explain: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot. The force is the same but the distance is larger, so the moment increases.

questions.q: A distance is 3 km. Calculate this distance in metres.
questions.explain: One kilometre is 1000 metres. So 3 km = 3 × 1000 m = 3000 m.

questions.q: A time is 30 min. Calculate this time in hours.
questions.explain: One hour is 60 minutes. So 30 min = 30 ÷ 60 h = 0.5 h.

questions.q: A time is 2 h. Calculate this time in minutes.
questions.explain: One hour is 60 minutes. So 2 h = 2 × 60 min = 120 min.

questions.q: A distance is 2500 m. Calculate this distance in kilometres.
questions.explain: One kilometre is 1000 metres. So 2500 m = 2500 ÷ 1000 km = 2.5 km.

questions.q: State the formula for speed.
questions.explain: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time. So speed = distance ÷ time.

questions.q: Speed is distance divided by time. Identify the formula for time.
questions.explain: Rearranging speed = distance ÷ time gives time = distance ÷ speed.

questions.q: A car travels 300 km in 2 h. Calculate its average speed.
questions.explain: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 300 km ÷ 2 h = 150 km/h.

questions.q: A runner runs 100 m in 20 s. Calculate the average speed.
questions.explain: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 100 m ÷ 20 s = 5 m/s.

questions.q: A girl walks at 2 m/s for 50 s. Calculate the distance she walks.
questions.explain: Distance = speed × time = 2 m/s × 50 s = 100 m.

questions.q: A car travels 45 km at 15 km/h. Calculate the time taken.
questions.explain: Time = distance ÷ speed = 45 km ÷ 15 km/h = 3 h.

questions.q: Define acceleration.
choices: the rate of change of speed
the time taken to speed up
questions.explain: Acceleration is the rate of change of speed. It tells us how much the speed changes every second.

questions.q: State the SI unit of acceleration.
questions.explain: Acceleration is the change in speed (m/s) per second, so its SI unit is metres per second squared (m/s²).

questions.q: A truck's speed increases by 6 m/s in 3 s. Calculate the acceleration.
questions.explain: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 6 m/s ÷ 3 s = 2 m/s².

questions.q: A car speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 s. Calculate the acceleration.
questions.explain: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = (20 - 0) m/s ÷ 5 s = 4 m/s².

questions.q: A bicycle slows down from 8 m/s to a stop in 2 s. Calculate its deceleration.
questions.explain: The speed falls by 8 m/s in 2 s. Deceleration = 8 m/s ÷ 2 s = 4 m/s².

questions.q: A car's speed increases by 10 m/s. Its acceleration is 2 m/s². Calculate the time taken.
questions.explain: Time = change in speed ÷ acceleration = 10 m/s ÷ 2 m/s² = 5 s.

questions.q: A distance-time graph is a horizontal line. Describe the motion of the object.
questions.explain: A horizontal line means the distance does not change as time passes. So the object is not moving.

questions.q: A distance-time graph is a straight sloping line. Describe the motion of the object.
questions.explain: A straight sloping line means the distance increases by the same amount every second. So the object moves at a constant speed.

questions.q: Two lines on a distance-time graph are compared. Identify what the steeper line shows.
questions.explain: The gradient of a distance-time graph shows the speed. A steeper line means more distance in each second, which is a higher speed.

questions.q: An object is not moving. Identify the shape of its distance-time graph.
questions.explain: An object that is not moving stays at the same distance, so its distance-time graph is a horizontal line.

questions.q: A distance-time graph shows a cyclist travels 20 m in 4 s. Calculate the average speed.
questions.explain: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 20 m ÷ 4 s = 5 m/s.

questions.q: A distance-time graph shows a speed of 2 m/s. Calculate the distance covered in 3 s.
questions.explain: Distance = speed × time = 2 m/s × 3 s = 6 m.

questions.q: A stone raises a measuring cylinder reading from 18 to 26 cm³. Calculate the stone's volume.
questions.explain: The stone pushes the water up by its own volume. Volume of stone = 26 cm³ - 18 cm³ = 8 cm³.

questions.q: A thermometer reads 25 °C, then 40 °C. Calculate the rise in temperature.
questions.explain: The rise in temperature is the final reading minus the first reading. Rise = 40 °C - 25 °C = 15 °C.

questions.q: A stopwatch reads 1 min 6 s. Calculate this time in seconds.
questions.explain: One minute is 60 seconds. So 1 min 6 s = 60 s + 6 s = 66 s.

questions.q: A pile of 5 identical blocks is 20 cm high. Calculate the height of one block.
questions.explain: The 5 identical blocks share the height equally. Height of one block = 20 cm ÷ 5 = 4 cm.
